The final result of running the reducer across all elements of the array is a single value.

what does array.reverse do in javascript | javascript array reverse | how do i use reverse on an array in js => The `reverse()` method of Array instances reverses an array in place and returns the reference to the same array, the first array element now becoming the last, and the last array element becoming the first. In other words, elements order in the array will be turned towards the direction opposite to that previously stated.

The original array will not be modified.

The default sort order is ascending, built upon converting the elements into strings, then comparing their sequences of UTF-16 code unit values.

To get the full Unicode code point at the given index, use .

what does string.raw do in javascript | javascript string raw | how do i use raw on a string in js => The `String.raw()` static method is a tag function of template literals. This is similar to the `r` prefix in Python, or the `@` prefix in C# for string literals. It's used to get the raw string form of template literals , that is, substitutions (e.g., `${foo}`) are processed, but escape sequences (e.g., `\n`) are not.

what does object.seal do in javascript | javascript object seal | how do i use object.seal in js => The `Object.seal()` static method seals an object. Sealing an object prevents extensions and makes existing properties non-configurable. A sealed object has a fixed set of properties: new properties cannot be added, existing properties cannot be removed, their enumerability and configurability cannot be changed, and its prototype cannot be re-assigned.

what does promise.all do in javascript | javascript promise all | how do i use promise.all in js => The `Promise.all()` static method takes an iterable of promises as input and returns a single Promise. This returned promise fulfills when all of the input's promises fulfill (including when an empty iterable is passed), with an array of the fulfillment values. It rejects when any of the input's promises rejects, with this first rejection reason.
what does promise.allsettled do in javascript | javascript promise allsettled | how do i use promise.allsettled in js => The `Promise.allSettled()` static method takes an iterable of promises as input and returns a single Promise. This returned promise fulfills when all of the input's promises settle (including when an empty iterable is passed), with an array of objects that describe the outcome of each promise.
what does promise.any do in javascript | javascript promise any | how do i use promise.any in js => The `Promise.any()` static method takes an iterable of promises as input and returns a single Promise. This returned promise fulfills when any of the input's promises fulfills, with this first fulfillment value.
what does promise.race do in javascript | javascript promise race | how do i use promise.race in js => The `Promise.race()` static method takes an iterable of promises as input and returns a single Promise. This returned promise settles with the eventual state of the first promise that settles.
what does promise.resolve do in javascript | javascript promise resolve | how do i use promise.resolve in js => The `Promise.resolve()` static method "resolves" a given value to a Promise. If the value is a promise, that promise is returned; if the value is a thenable, `Promise.resolve()` will call the `then()` method with two callbacks it prepared; otherwise the returned promise will be fulfilled with the value.
what does promise.reject do in javascript | javascript promise reject | how do i use promise.reject in js => The `Promise.reject()` static method returns a `Promise` object that is rejected with a given reason.
what does promise.then do in javascript | how do i use promise.then in js => The `then()` method of Promise instances takes up to two arguments: callback functions for the fulfilled and rejected cases of the `Promise`. It stores the callbacks within the promise it is called on and immediately returns another Promise object, allowing you to chain calls to other promise methods.
what does promise.catch do in javascript | javascript promise catch | how do i use promise.catch in js => The `catch()` method of Promise instances schedules a function to be called when the promise is rejected. It immediately returns another Promise object, allowing you to chain calls to other promise methods. It is a shortcut for .
what does promise.finally do in javascript | javascript promise finally | how do i use promise.finally in js => The `finally()` method of Promise instances schedules a function to be called when the promise is settled (either fulfilled or rejected). It immediately returns another Promise object, allowing you to chain calls to other promise methods.
what does promise.withresolvers do in javascript | javascript promise withresolvers | how do i use promise.withresolvers in js => The `Promise.withResolvers()` static method returns an object containing a new Promise object and two functions to resolve or reject it, corresponding to the two parameters passed to the executor of the constructor.
what does map.get do in javascript | javascript map get | how do i use get on a map in js => The `get()` method of Map instances returns the value corresponding to the key in this `Map`, or `undefined` if there is none. Object values are returned as the same reference that was originally stored, not as a copy, so mutations to the returned object will be reflected anywhere that reference is held, including inside the `Map`.
what does map.set do in javascript | javascript map set | how do i use set on a map in js => The `set()` method of Map instances adds a new entry with a specified key and value to this `Map`, or updates an existing entry if the key already exists.
what does map.delete do in javascript | javascript map delete | how do i use delete on a map in js => The `delete()` method of Map instances removes the entry specified by the key from this `Map`.
what does map.clear do in javascript | javascript map clear | how do i use clear on a map in js => The `clear()` method of Map instances removes all elements from this map.
what does map.size do in javascript | javascript map size | how do i use size on a map in js => The `size` accessor property of Map instances returns the number of elements in this map.
what does map.foreach do in javascript | javascript map foreach | how do i use foreach on a map in js => The `forEach()` method of Map instances executes a provided function once per each key/value pair in this map, in insertion order.
what does set.add do in javascript | javascript set add | how do i use add on a set in js => The `add()` method of Set instances inserts the specified value into this set, if it is not already present.
what does set.has do in javascript | javascript set has | how do i use has on a set in js => The `has()` method of Set instances returns a boolean indicating whether the specified value exists in this `Set` or not.
what does set.delete do in javascript | javascript set delete | how do i use delete on a set in js => The `delete()` method of Set instances removes the specified value from this set, if it is in the set.
what does set.clear do in javascript | javascript set clear | how do i use clear on a set in js => The `clear()` method of Set instances removes all elements from this set.
what does set.size do in javascript | javascript set size | how do i use size on a set in js => The `size` accessor property of Set instances returns the number of (unique) elements in this set.
what does set.union do in javascript | javascript set union | how do i use union on a set in js => The `union()` method of Set instances takes a set and returns a new set containing elements which are in either or both of this set and the given set.
what does set.intersection do in javascript | javascript set intersection | how do i use intersection on a set in js => The `intersection()` method of Set instances takes a set and returns a new set containing elements in both this set and the given set.
what does set.difference do in javascript | javascript set difference | how do i use difference on a set in js => The `difference()` method of Set instances takes a set and returns a new set containing elements in this set but not in the given set.
what does date.now do in javascript | javascript date now | how do i use now on a date in js => The `Date.now()` static method returns the number of milliseconds elapsed since the epoch, which is defined as the midnight at the beginning of January 1, 1970, UTC.
what does date.getfullyear do in javascript | javascript date getfullyear | how do i use getfullyear on a date in js => The `getFullYear()` method of Date instances returns the year for this date according to local time. Use this method instead of the method.
what does date.getmonth do in javascript | javascript date getmonth | how do i use getmonth on a date in js => The `getMonth()` method of Date instances returns the month for this date according to local time, as a zero-based value (where zero indicates the first month of the year).
what does date.getdate do in javascript | javascript date getdate | how do i use getdate on a date in js => The `getDate()` method of Date instances returns the day of the month for this date according to local time.
what does date.getday do in javascript | javascript date getday | how do i use getday on a date in js => The `getDay()` method of Date instances returns the day of the week for this date according to local time, where 0 represents Sunday. For the day of the month, see .
what does date.gethours do in javascript | javascript date gethours | how do i use gethours on a date in js => The `getHours()` method of Date instances returns the hours for this date according to local time.
what does date.getminutes do in javascript | javascript date getminutes | how do i use getminutes on a date in js => The `getMinutes()` method of Date instances returns the minutes for this date according to local time.
what does date.gettime do in javascript | javascript date gettime | how do i use gettime on a date in js => The `getTime()` method of Date instances returns the number of milliseconds for this date since the epoch, which is defined as the midnight at the beginning of January 1, 1970, UTC.
what does date.toisostring do in javascript | javascript date toisostring | how do i use toisostring on a date in js => The `toISOString()` method of Date instances returns a string representing this date in the date time string format, a simplified format based on ISO 8601, which is always 24 or 27 characters long (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ` or `±YYYYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ`, respectively). The timezone is always UTC, as denoted by the suffix `Z`.
what does date.tolocaledatestring do in javascript | javascript date tolocaledatestring | how do i use tolocaledatestring on a date in js => The `toLocaleDateString()` method of Date instances returns a string with a language-sensitive representation of the date portion of this date in the local timezone. In implementations with `Intl.DateTimeFormat` API support, this method delegates to `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.
what does parseint do in javascript | javascript parseint function | how do i use parseint in js => The `parseInt()` function parses a string argument and returns an integer of the specified radix (the base in mathematical numeral systems).
what does parsefloat do in javascript | javascript parsefloat function | how do i use parsefloat in js => The `parseFloat()` function parses a string argument and returns a floating point number.
what does isnan do in javascript | javascript isnan function | how do i use isnan in js => The `isNaN()` function determines whether a value is NaN, first converting the value to a number if necessary. Because coercion inside the `isNaN()` function can be surprising, you may prefer to use .
what does encodeuricomponent do in javascript | javascript encodeuricomponent function | how do i use encodeuricomponent in js => The `encodeURIComponent()` function encodes a URI by replacing each instance of certain characters by one, two, three, or four escape sequences representing the UTF-8 encoding of the character (will only be four escape sequences for characters composed of two surrogate characters).
what does decodeuricomponent do in javascript | javascript decodeuricomponent function | how do i use decodeuricomponent in js => The `decodeURIComponent()` function decodes a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI) component previously created by or by a similar routine.
what does globalthis do in javascript | javascript globalthis function | how do i use globalthis in js => The `globalThis` global property contains the global `this` value, which is usually akin to the global object.
javascript array object | js array explained => The `Array` object, as with arrays in other programming languages, enables storing a collection of multiple items under a single variable name, and has members for performing common array operations.
javascript string object | js string explained => The `String` object is used to represent and manipulate a sequence of characters.
what is math in javascript | javascript math object | js math explained => The `Math` namespace object contains static properties and methods for mathematical constants and functions. `Math` works with the Number type. It doesn't work with BigInt.
what is number in javascript | javascript number object | js number explained => `Number` values represent floating-point numbers like `37` or `-9.25`. The `Number` constructor contains constants and methods for working with numbers. Values of other types can be converted to numbers using the `Number()` function.
what is json in javascript | javascript json object | js json explained => The `JSON` namespace object contains static methods for parsing values from and converting values to JavaScript Object Notation (JSON).
javascript promise object | js promise explained => The `Promise` object represents the eventual completion (or failure) of an asynchronous operation and its resulting value. To learn about the way promises work and how you can use them, we advise you to read Using promises first.
javascript map object | js map explained => The `Map` object holds key-value pairs and remembers the original insertion order of the keys. Any value (both objects and primitive values) may be used as either a key or a value.
javascript set object | js set explained => The `Set` object lets you store unique values of any type, whether primitive values or object references.
what is weakmap in javascript | javascript weakmap object | js weakmap explained => A `WeakMap` is a collection of key/value pairs whose keys must be objects or non-registered symbols, with values of any arbitrary JavaScript type, and which does not create strong references to its keys. That is, an object's presence as a key in a `WeakMap` does not prevent the object from being garbage collected.
what is date in javascript | javascript date object | js date explained => JavaScript `Date` objects represent a single moment in time in a platform-independent format. `Date` objects encapsulate an integral number that represents milliseconds since the midnight at the beginning of January 1, 1970, UTC (the epoch).
what is regexp in javascript | javascript regexp object | js regexp explained => The `RegExp` object is used for matching text with a pattern. For an introduction to regular expressions, read the Regular expressions chapter in the JavaScript guide. For detailed information of regular expression syntax, read the regular expression reference.
what is symbol in javascript | javascript symbol object | js symbol explained => `Symbol` is a built-in object whose constructor returns a `symbol` primitive , also called a Symbol value or just a Symbol , that's guaranteed to be unique.
what is bigint in javascript | javascript bigint object | js bigint explained => `BigInt` values represent integer values which are too high or too low to be represented by the `number` primitive.
what is error in javascript | javascript error object | js error explained => `Error` objects are thrown when runtime errors occur. The `Error` object can also be used as a base object for user-defined exceptions.
what is typeerror in javascript | javascript typeerror object | js typeerror explained => The `TypeError` object represents an error when an operation could not be performed, typically (but not exclusively) when a value is not of the expected type.
what is syntaxerror in javascript | javascript syntaxerror object | js syntaxerror explained => The `SyntaxError` object represents an error when trying to interpret syntactically invalid code. It is thrown when the JavaScript engine encounters tokens or token order that does not conform to the syntax of the language when parsing code.
what is rangeerror in javascript | javascript rangeerror object | js rangeerror explained => The `RangeError` object indicates an error when a value is not in the set or range of allowed values.
what is referenceerror in javascript | javascript referenceerror object | js referenceerror explained => `ReferenceError` is a serializable object, so it can be cloned with or copied between Workers using .
what is boolean in javascript | javascript boolean object | js boolean explained => `Boolean` values can be one of two values: `true` or `false`, representing the truth value of a logical proposition.
what is function in javascript | javascript function object | js function explained => The `Function` object provides methods for functions. In JavaScript, every function is actually a `Function` object.
what is proxy in javascript | javascript proxy object | js proxy explained => The `Proxy` object enables you to create a proxy for another object, which can intercept and redefine fundamental operations for that object.
what is reflect in javascript | javascript reflect object | js reflect explained => The `Reflect` namespace object contains static methods for invoking interceptable JavaScript object internal methods. The methods are the same as those of proxy handlers.
what is intl in javascript | javascript intl object | js intl explained => The `Intl` namespace object contains several constructors as well as functionality common to the internationalization constructors and other language sensitive functions. Collectively, they comprise the ECMAScript Internationalization API, which provides language sensitive string comparison, number formatting, date and time formatting, and more.
what is nullish coalescing in javascript | javascript nullish coalescing | how does nullish coalescing work in js => The nullish coalescing (`??`) operator is a logical operator that returns its right-hand side operand when its left-hand side operand is `null` or undefined, and otherwise returns its left-hand side operand.
what is optional chaining in javascript | javascript optional chaining | how does optional chaining work in js => The optional chaining (`?.`) operator accesses an object's property or calls a function. If the object accessed or function called using this operator is undefined or `null`, the expression short circuits and evaluates to undefined instead of throwing an error.
what is spread syntax in javascript | javascript spread syntax | how does spread syntax work in js => The spread (`...`) syntax allows an iterable, such as an array or string, to be expanded in places where zero or more arguments (for function calls) or elements (for array literals) are expected. In an object literal, the spread syntax enumerates the properties of an object and adds the key-value pairs to the object being created.
what is destructuring in javascript | javascript destructuring | how does destructuring work in js => The destructuring syntax is a JavaScript syntax that makes it possible to unpack values from arrays, or properties from objects, into distinct variables. It can be used in locations that receive data (such as the left-hand side of an assignment or anywhere that creates new identifier bindings).
what is conditional operator in javascript | javascript conditional operator | how does conditional operator work in js => The conditional (ternary) operator is the only JavaScript operator that takes three operands: a condition followed by a question mark (`?`), then an expression to execute if the condition is truthy followed by a colon (`:`), and finally the expression to execute if the condition is falsy.
what is typeof in javascript | javascript typeof | how does typeof work in js => The `typeof` operator returns a string indicating the type of the operand's value.
what is instanceof in javascript | javascript instanceof | how does instanceof work in js => The `instanceof` operator tests to see if the `prototype` property of a constructor appears anywhere in the prototype chain of an object. The return value is a boolean value. Its behavior can be customized with `Symbol.hasInstance`.
what is strict equality in javascript | javascript strict equality | how does strict equality work in js => The strict equality (`===`) operator checks whether its two operands are equal, returning a Boolean result. Unlike the equality operator, the strict equality operator always considers operands of different types to be different.
what is equality in javascript | javascript equality | how does equality work in js => The equality (`==`) operator checks whether its two operands are equal, returning a Boolean result. Unlike the strict equality operator, it attempts to convert and compare operands that are of different types.
what is await in javascript | javascript await | how does await work in js => The `await` operator is used to wait for a Promise and get its fulfillment value. It can only be used inside an async function or at the top level of a module.
what is new in javascript | javascript new | how does new work in js => The `new` operator lets developers create an instance of a user-defined object type or of one of the built-in object types that has a constructor function.
what is this in javascript | javascript this | how does this work in js => The `this` keyword refers to the context where a piece of code, such as a function's body, is supposed to run. Most typically, it is used in object methods, where `this` refers to the object that the method is attached to, thus allowing the same method to be reused on different objects.
what is delete in javascript | javascript delete | how does delete work in js => The `delete` operator removes a property from an object. If the property's value is an object and there are no more references to the object, the object held by that property is eventually released automatically.
what is in in javascript | javascript in => The `in` operator returns `true` if the specified property is in the specified object or its prototype chain. The `in` operator cannot be used to search for values in other collections. To test if a certain value exists in an array, use . For sets, use .
what is remainder in javascript | javascript remainder | how does remainder work in js => The remainder (`%`) operator returns the remainder left over when one operand is divided by a second operand. It always takes the sign of the dividend.
what is exponentiation in javascript | javascript exponentiation | how does exponentiation work in js => The exponentiation (``) operator returns the result of raising the first operand to the power of the second operand. It is equivalent to , except it also accepts BigInts as operands.
what is logical not in javascript | javascript logical not | how does logical not work in js => The logical NOT (`!`) (logical complement, negation) operator takes truth to falsity and vice versa. It is typically used with boolean (logical) values. When used with non-Boolean values, it returns `false` if its single operand can be converted to `true`; otherwise, returns `true`.
what is comma operator in javascript | javascript comma operator | how does comma operator work in js => The comma (`,`) operator evaluates each of its operands (from left to right) and returns the value of the last operand. This is commonly used to provide multiple updaters to a `for` loop's afterthought.
what is let in javascript | javascript let => The `let` declaration declares re-assignable, block-scoped local variables, optionally initializing each to a value.
what is const in javascript | javascript const | how does const work in js => The `const` declaration declares block-scoped local variables. The value of a constant can't be changed through reassignment using the assignment operator, but if a constant is an object, its properties can be added, updated, or removed.
what is var in javascript | javascript var | how does var work in js => The `var` statement declares function-scoped or globally-scoped variables, optionally initializing each to a value.
what is for of in javascript | javascript for of => The `for...of` statement executes a loop that operates on a sequence of values sourced from an iterable object. Iterable objects include instances of built-ins such as Array, String, TypedArray, Map, Set, NodeList (and other DOM collections), as well as the arguments object, generators produced by generator functions, and user-defined iterables.
what is for in in javascript | javascript for in => The `for...in` statement iterates over all enumerable string properties of an object (ignoring properties keyed by symbols), including inherited enumerable properties.
what is switch in javascript | javascript switch | how does switch work in js => The `switch` statement evaluates an expression, matching the expression's value against a series of `case` clauses, and executes statements after the first `case` clause with a matching value, until a `break` statement is encountered. The `default` clause of a `switch` statement will be jumped to if no `case` matches the expression's value.
what is try catch in javascript | javascript try catch | how does try catch work in js => The `try...catch` statement is comprised of a `try` block and either a `catch` block, a `finally` block, or both. The code in the `try` block is executed first, and if it throws an exception, the code in the `catch` block will be executed. The code in the `finally` block will always be executed before control flow exits the entire construct.
what is throw in javascript | javascript throw | how does throw work in js => The `throw` statement throws a user-defined exception. If no `catch` block exists among caller functions, the program will terminate.
what is class in javascript | javascript class | how does class work in js => The `class` declaration creates a binding of a new class to a given name. You can also define classes using the `class` expression.
what is async function in javascript | javascript async function | how does async function work in js => The `async function` declaration creates a binding of a new async function to a given name. The `await` keyword is permitted within the function body, enabling asynchronous, promise-based behavior to be written in a cleaner style and avoiding the need to explicitly configure promise chains.
what is import in javascript | javascript import | how does import work in js => The static `import` declaration is used to import read-only live bindings which are exported by another module. The imported bindings are called live bindings because they are updated by the module that exported the binding, but cannot be re-assigned by the importing module.
what is export in javascript | javascript export | how does export work in js => The `export` declaration is used to export values from a JavaScript module. Exported values can then be imported into other programs with the import declaration or dynamic import.
what is break in javascript | javascript break | how does break work in js => It can also be used to jump past a labeled statement when used within that labeled statement.
what is do while in javascript | javascript do while | how does do while work in js => The `do...while` statement creates a loop that executes a specified statement as long as the test condition evaluates to true. The condition is evaluated after executing the statement, resulting in the specified statement executing at least once.
what is label in javascript | javascript label | how does label work in js => A labeled statement is any statement that is prefixed with an identifier. You can jump to this label using a break or continue statement nested within the labeled statement.
what is default parameters in javascript | javascript default parameters | how does default parameters work in js => Default function parameters allow named parameters to be initialized with default values if no value or `undefined` is passed.
what is rest parameters in javascript | javascript rest parameters | how does rest parameters work in js => The rest parameter syntax allows a function to accept an indefinite number of arguments as an array, providing a way to represent variadic functions in JavaScript.
what is get in javascript | javascript get => The `get` syntax binds an object property to a function that will be called when that property is looked up. It can also be used in classes.
what is template literals in javascript | javascript template literals | how does template literals work in js => Template literals are literals delimited with backtick (`` ` ``) characters, allowing for multi-line strings, string interpolation with embedded expressions, and special constructs called tagged templates.
what is strict mode in javascript | javascript strict mode | how does strict mode work in js => JavaScript's strict mode is a way to opt in to a restricted variant of JavaScript, thereby implicitly opting-out of "sloppy mode". Strict mode isn't just a subset: it intentionally has different semantics from normal code. Strict mode code and non-strict mode code can coexist, so scripts can opt into strict mode incrementally.
what is constructor in javascript | javascript constructor | how does constructor work in js => The `constructor` method is a special method of a class for creating and initializing an object instance of that class.
what is extends in javascript | javascript extends | how does extends work in js => The `extends` keyword is used in class declarations or class expressions to create a class that is a child of another class.
what is static in javascript | javascript static | how does static work in js => The `static` keyword defines a static method or field for a class, or a static initialization block (see the link for more information about this usage). Static properties cannot be directly accessed on instances of the class. Instead, they're accessed on the class itself.
what is private elements in javascript | javascript private elements | how does private elements work in js => Private elements are counterparts of the regular class elements which are public, including class fields, class methods, etc. Private elements get created by using a hash `#` prefix and cannot be legally referenced outside of the class. The privacy encapsulation of these class elements is enforced by JavaScript itself.
# tag: coding.web.css
what does margin do in css | css margin property | how do i use margin in css => The `margin` CSS shorthand property sets the margin area on all four sides of an element.
what does padding do in css | css padding property | how do i use padding in css => The `padding` CSS shorthand property sets the padding area on all four sides of an element at once.
what does border do in css | css border property | how do i use border in css => The `border` CSS shorthand property sets an element's border. It sets the values of border-width, border-style, and border-color.
what does border-radius do in css | css border-radius property | how do i use border radius in css => The `border-radius` CSS shorthand property rounds the corners of an element's outer border edge. You can set a single radius to make circular corners, or two radii to make elliptical corners.
what does width do in css | css width property | how do i use width in css => The `width` CSS property sets an element's width. By default, it sets the width of the content area, but if box-sizing is set to `border-box`, it sets the width of the border area.
what does height do in css | css height property | how do i use height in css => The `height` CSS property specifies the height of an element. By default, the property defines the height of the content area. If box-sizing is set to `border-box`, however, it instead determines the height of the border area.
what does max-width do in css | css max-width property | how do i use max width in css => The `max-width` CSS property sets the maximum width of an element. It prevents the used value of the width property from becoming larger than the value specified by `max-width`.
what does min-width do in css | css min-width property | how do i use min width in css => The `min-width` CSS property sets the minimum width of an element. It prevents the used value of the width property from becoming smaller than the value specified for `min-width`.
what does max-height do in css | css max-height property | how do i use max height in css => The `max-height` CSS property sets the maximum height of an element. It prevents the used value of the height property from becoming larger than the value specified for `max-height`.
what does min-height do in css | css min-height property | how do i use min height in css => The `min-height` CSS property sets the minimum height of an element. It prevents the used value of the height property from becoming smaller than the value specified for `min-height`.
what does color do in css | css color property | how do i use color in css => The `color` CSS property sets the foreground color value of an element's text and text decorations, and sets the `currentColor` value. `currentColor` may be used as an indirect value on other properties and is the default for other color properties, such as border-color.
what does background do in css | css background property | how do i use background in css => The `background` CSS shorthand property sets all background style properties at once, such as color, image, origin, size, and repeat method.
what does background-color do in css | css background-color property | how do i use background color in css => The `background-color` CSS property sets the background color of an element.
what does background-image do in css | css background-image property | how do i use background image in css => The `background-image` CSS property sets one or more background images on an element.
what does background-size do in css | css background-size property | how do i use background size in css => The `background-size` CSS property sets the size of the element's background image. The image can be left to its natural size, stretched, or constrained to fit the available space.
what does background-position do in css | css background-position property | how do i use background position in css => The `background-position` CSS property sets the initial position for each background image.
what does background-repeat do in css | css background-repeat property | how do i use background repeat in css => The `background-repeat` CSS shorthand property sets how background images are repeated. A background image can be repeated along the horizontal and vertical axes, or not repeated at all.
what does font-family do in css | css font-family property | how do i use font family in css => The `font-family` CSS property specifies a prioritized list of one or more font family names and/or generic family names for the selected element.
what does font-size do in css | css font-size property | how do i use font size in css => The `font-size` CSS property sets the size of the font. Changing the font size also updates the sizes of the font size-relative <length> units, such as `em`, `ex`, and so forth.
what does font-weight do in css | css font-weight property | how do i use font weight in css => The `font-weight` CSS property sets the weight (or boldness) of the font.
what does font-style do in css | css font-style property | how do i use font style in css => The `font-style` CSS property sets whether a font should be styled with a normal, italic, or oblique face from its font-family.
what does line-height do in css | css line-height property | how do i use line height in css => The `line-height` CSS property sets the height of a line box in horizontal writing modes. In vertical writing modes, it sets the width of a line box. It's commonly used to set the distance between lines of text.
what does letter-spacing do in css | css letter-spacing property | how do i use letter spacing in css => The `letter-spacing` CSS property sets the spacing between text characters. This value is added to the natural spacing between characters while rendering the text. Positive values of `letter-spacing` spread characters further apart, while negative values of `letter-spacing` bring characters closer together.
what does text-align do in css | css text-align property | how do i use text align in css => The `text-align` CSS property sets the horizontal alignment of the inline-level content inside a block element or table-cell box. This means it works like vertical-align but in the horizontal direction.
what does text-decoration do in css | css text-decoration property | how do i use text decoration in css => The `text-decoration` CSS shorthand property sets the appearance of decorative lines on text. It is a shorthand for text-decoration-line, text-decoration-color, text-decoration-style, and the newer text-decoration-thickness property.
what does text-transform do in css | css text-transform property | how do i use text transform in css => The `text-transform` CSS property specifies how to capitalize an element's text. It can be used to make text appear in all-uppercase or all-lowercase, or with each word capitalized. It also can help improve legibility for ruby.
what does text-shadow do in css | css text-shadow property | how do i use text shadow in css => The `text-shadow` CSS property adds shadows to text. It accepts a comma-separated list of shadows to be applied to the text and any of its text-decoration. Each shadow is described by some combination of X and Y offsets from the element, blur radius, and color.
what does white-space do in css | css white-space property | how do i use white space in css => The `white-space` CSS shorthand property sets how white space inside an element is handled.
what does word-break do in css | css word-break property | how do i use word break in css => The `word-break` CSS property sets whether line breaks appear wherever the text would otherwise overflow its content box.
what does overflow do in css | css overflow property | how do i use overflow in css => The `overflow` CSS shorthand property sets the desired behavior when content does not fit in the element's padding box (overflows) in the horizontal and/or vertical direction.
what does overflow-wrap do in css | css overflow-wrap property | how do i use overflow wrap in css => The `overflow-wrap` CSS property applies to text, setting whether the browser should insert line breaks within an otherwise unbreakable string to prevent text from overflowing its line box.
what does display do in css | css display property | how do i use display in css => The `display` CSS property sets whether an element is treated as a block or inline box and the layout used for its children, such as flow layout, grid or flex.
what does position do in css | css position property | how do i use position in css => The `position` CSS property sets how an element is positioned in a document. The top, right, bottom, and left physical properties and the inset-block-start, inset-block-end, inset-inline-start, and inset-inline-end flow-relative logical properties can be used to determine the final location of positioned elements.
what does top do in css | css top property | how do i use top in css => The `top` CSS property sets the vertical position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.
what does left do in css | css left property | how do i use left in css => The `left` CSS property participates in specifying the horizontal position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.
what does right do in css | css right property | how do i use right in css => The `right` CSS property participates in specifying the horizontal position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.
what does bottom do in css | css bottom property | how do i use bottom in css => The `bottom` CSS property participates in setting the vertical position of a positioned element. This inset property has no effect on non-positioned elements.
what does z-index do in css | css z-index property | how do i use z index in css => The `z-index` CSS property sets the z-order of a positioned element and its descendants or flex and grid items. Overlapping elements with a larger z-index cover those with a smaller one.
what does float do in css | css float property | how do i use float in css => The `float` CSS property places an element on the left or right side of its container, allowing text and inline elements to wrap around it. The element is removed from the normal flow of the page, though still remaining a part of the flow (in contrast to absolute positioning).
what does clear do in css | css clear property | how do i use clear in css => The `clear` property applies to floating and non-floating elements.
what does flex do in css | css flex property | how do i use flex in css => The `flex` CSS shorthand property sets how a flex item will grow or shrink to fit the space available in its flex container.
what does flex-direction do in css | css flex-direction property | how do i use flex direction in css => The `flex-direction` CSS property sets how flex items are placed in the flex container defining the main axis and the direction (normal or reversed).
what does flex-wrap do in css | css flex-wrap property | how do i use flex wrap in css => The `flex-wrap` CSS property sets whether flex items are forced onto one line or can wrap onto multiple lines. If wrapping is allowed, it sets the direction that lines are stacked.
what does justify-content do in css | css justify-content property | how do i use justify content in css => The CSS `justify-content` property defines how the browser distributes space between and around content items along the main axis of a flex container and the inline axis of grid and multicol containers.
what does align-items do in css | css align-items property | how do i use align items in css => The CSS `align-items` property sets the align-self value on all direct children as a group. In flexbox, it controls the alignment of items on the cross axis. In grid layout, it controls the alignment of items on the block axis within their grid areas.
what does align-content do in css | css align-content property | how do i use align content in css => The CSS `align-content` property sets the distribution of space between and around content items along a flexbox's cross axis, or a grid or block-level element's block axis.
what does align-self do in css | css align-self property | how do i use align self in css => The `align-self` CSS property overrides a grid or flex item's align-items value. In grid, it aligns the item inside the grid area. In flexbox, it aligns the item on the cross axis.
what does flex-grow do in css | css flex-grow property | how do i use flex grow in css => The `flex-grow` CSS property sets the flex grow factor, which specifies how much of the flex container's positive free space, if any, should be assigned to the flex item's main size.
what does flex-shrink do in css | css flex-shrink property | how do i use flex shrink in css => The `flex-shrink` CSS property sets the flex shrink factor of a flex item. If the size of all flex items is larger than the flex container, the flex items can shrink to fit according to their `flex-shrink` value. Each flex line's negative free space is distributed between the line's flex items that have a `flex-shrink` value greater than `0`.
what does flex-basis do in css | css flex-basis property | how do i use flex basis in css => The `flex-basis` CSS property sets the initial main size of a flex item. It sets the size of the content box unless otherwise set with box-sizing.
what does gap do in css | css gap property | how do i use gap in css => The `gap` CSS shorthand property sets the gaps (also called gutters) between rows and columns on multi-column, flex, and grid containers.
what does order do in css | css order property | how do i use order in css => The `order` CSS property sets the order to lay out an item in a flex or grid container. Items in a container are sorted by ascending `order` value and then by their source code order. Items not given an explicit `order` value are assigned the default value of `0`.
what does grid do in css | css grid property | how do i use grid in css => The `grid` CSS shorthand property sets all of the explicit and implicit grid properties in a single declaration.
what does grid-template-columns do in css | css grid-template-columns property | how do i use grid template columns in css => The `grid-template-columns` CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid columns.
what does grid-template-rows do in css | css grid-template-rows property | how do i use grid template rows in css => The `grid-template-rows` CSS property defines the line names and track sizing functions of the grid rows.
what does grid-template-areas do in css | css grid-template-areas property | how do i use grid template areas in css => The `grid-template-areas` CSS property specifies named grid areas, establishing the cells in the grid and assigning them names.
what does grid-column do in css | css grid-column property | how do i use grid column in css => The `grid-column` CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid column by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start and inline-end edge of its grid area.
what does grid-row do in css | css grid-row property | how do i use grid row in css => The `grid-row` CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid row by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the inline-start and inline-end edge of its grid area.
what does grid-area do in css | css grid-area property | how do i use grid area in css => The `grid-area` CSS shorthand property specifies a grid item's size and location within a grid by contributing a line, a span, or nothing (automatic) to its grid placement, thereby specifying the edges of its grid area.
what does place-items do in css | css place-items property | how do i use place items in css => The `place-items` CSS shorthand property aligns items along both block and inline directions at the same time.
what does opacity do in css | css opacity property | how do i use opacity in css => The `opacity` CSS property sets the opacity of an element. Opacity is the degree to which content behind an element is hidden, and is the opposite of transparency.
what does visibility do in css | css visibility property | how do i use visibility in css => The `visibility` CSS property shows or hides an element without changing the layout of a document. The property can also hide rows or columns in a <table>.
what does cursor do in css | css cursor property | how do i use cursor in css => The `cursor` CSS property sets the mouse cursor, if any, to show when the mouse pointer is over an element. You can specify either the type of cursor using a keyword, or load a specific icon to use (with optional fallback images and mandatory keyword as a final fallback).
what does box-shadow do in css | css box-shadow property | how do i use box shadow in css => The `box-shadow` CSS property adds shadow effects around an element's frame. You can set multiple effects separated by commas. A box shadow is described by X and Y offsets relative to the element, blur and spread radius, and color.
what does box-sizing do in css | css box-sizing property | how do i use box sizing in css => The `box-sizing` CSS property sets how the total width and height of an element is calculated.
what does transform do in css | css transform property | how do i use transform in css => The `transform` CSS property lets you rotate, scale, skew, or translate an element. It modifies the coordinate space of the CSS visual formatting model.
what does transition do in css | css transition property | how do i use transition in css => The `transition` CSS shorthand property for transition-property, transition-duration, transition-timing-function, transition-delay, and transition-behavior.
what does transition-duration do in css | css transition-duration property | how do i use transition duration in css => The `transition-duration` CSS property sets the length of time a transition animation should take to complete. By default, the value is `0s`, meaning that no animation will occur.
what does animation do in css | css animation property | how do i use animation in css => The `animation` CSS shorthand property applies an animation between styles. It is a shorthand for animation-name, animation-duration, animation-timing-function, animation-delay, animation-iteration-count, animation-direction, animation-fill-mode, animation-play-state, and animation-timeline.
what does animation-name do in css | css animation-name property | how do i use animation name in css => The `animation-name` CSS property specifies the names of one or more @keyframes at-rules that describe the animation to apply to an element. Multiple `@keyframes` at-rules are specified as a comma-separated list of names. If the specified name does not match any `@keyframes` at-rule, no properties are animated.
what does animation-duration do in css | css animation-duration property | how do i use animation duration in css => The `animation-duration` CSS property sets the length of time that an animation takes to complete one cycle. It is often convenient to use the shorthand property animation to set all animation properties at once.
what does filter do in css | css filter property | how do i use filter in css => The `filter` CSS property applies graphical effects like blur or color shift to an element. Filters are commonly used to adjust the rendering of images, backgrounds, and borders.
what does backdrop-filter do in css | css backdrop-filter property | how do i use backdrop filter in css => The `backdrop-filter` CSS property lets you apply graphical effects such as blurring or color shifting to the area behind an element. Because it applies to everything behind the element, to see the effect the element or its background needs to be transparent or partially transparent.
what does object-fit do in css | css object-fit property | how do i use object fit in css => The `object-fit` CSS property sets how the content of a replaced element, such as an <img> or <video>, should be resized to fit its container.
what does aspect-ratio do in css | css aspect-ratio property | how do i use aspect ratio in css => The `aspect-ratio` CSS property allows you to define the desired width-to-height ratio of an element's box.
what does outline do in css | css outline property | how do i use outline in css => The `outline` CSS shorthand property sets the style, color, and width of an element's outline.
what does list-style do in css | css list-style property | how do i use list style in css => The `list-style` CSS shorthand property allows you to set all the list style properties at once.
what does user-select do in css | css user-select property | how do i use user select in css => The `user-select` CSS property controls whether the user can select text. This doesn't have any effect on content loaded as part of a browser's user interface (its chrome), except in textboxes.
what does pointer-events do in css | css pointer-events property | how do i use pointer events in css => The `pointer-events` CSS property sets under what circumstances (if any) a particular graphic element can become the target of pointer events.
what does content do in css | css content property | how do i use content in css => The `content` CSS property replaces content with a generated value. It can be used to define what is rendered inside an element or pseudo-element. For elements, the `content` property specifies whether the element renders normally (`normal` or `none`) or is replaced with an image (and associated "alt" text).
what does vertical-align do in css | css vertical-align property | how do i use vertical align in css => The `vertical-align` CSS shorthand property sets the vertical alignment of an inline, inline-block, or table-cell box.
what does inset do in css | css inset property | how do i use inset in css => The `inset` CSS shorthand property corresponds to the top, right, bottom, and/or left properties. It has the same multi-value syntax of the margin shorthand.
what does clip-path do in css | css clip-path property | how do i use clip path in css => The `clip-path` CSS property creates a clipping region that sets what part of an element should be shown. Parts that are inside the region are shown, while those outside are hidden.
what does mix-blend-mode do in css | css mix-blend-mode property | how do i use mix blend mode in css => The `mix-blend-mode` CSS property sets how an element's content should blend with its backdrop , the content rendered behind the element within the same stacking context.
what does scroll-behavior do in css | css scroll-behavior property | how do i use scroll behavior in css => The `scroll-behavior` CSS property sets the behavior for a scrolling box when scrolling is triggered by the navigation or CSSOM scrolling APIs.
what does resize do in css | css resize property | how do i use resize in css => The `resize` CSS property sets whether an element is resizable, and if so, in which directions.
what does accent-color do in css | css accent-color property | how do i use accent color in css => The `accent-color` CSS property sets the accent color for user-interface controls generated by some elements.
what does text-overflow do in css | css text-overflow property | how do i use text overflow in css => The `text-overflow` CSS property sets how hidden overflow content is signaled to users.
what does column-count do in css | css column-count property | how do i use column count in css => The `column-count` CSS property breaks an element's content into the specified number of columns.
what does isolation do in css | css isolation property | how do i use isolation in css => The `isolation` CSS property determines whether an element must create a new stacking context. This property is especially helpful when used in conjunction with mix-blend-mode and z-index.
what does will-change do in css | css will-change property | how do i use will change in css => The `will-change` CSS property enables optimizing animations by providing a rendering hint to a browser about how an element is expected to change.
what is @media in css | css media | how do i use media in css => The `@media` CSS at-rule can be used to apply part of a style sheet based on the result of one or more media queries. With it, you specify a media query and a block of CSS to apply to the document if and only if the media query matches the device on which the content is being used.
what is @keyframes in css | css keyframes | how do i use keyframes in css => The `@keyframes` CSS at-rule controls the intermediate steps in a CSS animation sequence by defining styles for keyframes (or waypoints) along the animation sequence. This gives more control over the intermediate steps of the animation sequence than transitions.
what is @import in css | css import | how do i use import in css => The `@import` CSS at-rule is used to import style rules from other valid stylesheets. An `@import` rule must be defined at the top of the stylesheet, before any other at-rule (except @charset and @layer) and style declarations, or it will be ignored.
what is @font-face in css | css font face | how do i use font face in css => The `@font-face` CSS at-rule specifies a custom font with which to display text; the font can be loaded from either a remote server or a locally-installed font on the user's own computer.
what is calc in css | css calc | how do i use calc in css => The `calc()` CSS function lets you perform calculations when specifying CSS property values. It can be used with <length>, <frequency>, angle, <time>, <percentage>, <number>, <integer>, and <color-function> values.
what is var in css | css var | how do i use var in css => The `var()` CSS function can be used to insert the value of a custom property (sometimes called a "CSS variable") instead of any part of a value of another property.
what is clamp in css | css clamp | how do i use clamp in css => The `clamp()` CSS function clamps a value within a range of values between a defined minimum bound and a maximum bound. The function takes three parameters: a minimum value, a preferred value, and a maximum allowed value.
what is min in css | css min | how do i use min in css => The `min()` CSS function lets you set the smallest (most negative) value from a list of comma-separated expressions as the value of a CSS property value. The `min()` function can be used anywhere a <length>, <frequency>, angle, <time>, <percentage>, <number>, or <integer> is allowed.
what is max in css | css max | how do i use max in css => The `max()` CSS function lets you set the largest (most positive) value from a list of comma-separated expressions as the value of a CSS property value. The `max()` function can be used anywhere a <length>, <frequency>, angle, <time>, <percentage>, <number>, or <integer> is allowed.
what is :hover in css | css hover | how do i use hover in css => The `:hover` CSS pseudo-class matches an element when a user interacts with it using a pointing device. The pseudo-class is generally triggered when the user moves the cursor (mouse pointer) over an element without pressing the mouse button.
what is :focus in css | css focus | how do i use focus in css => The `:focus` CSS pseudo-class represents an element (such as a form input) that has received focus. It is generally triggered when the user clicks or taps on an element or selects it with the keyboard's <kbd>Tab</kbd> key.
what is :active in css | css active | how do i use active in css => The `:active` CSS pseudo-class represents an element (such as a button) that is being activated by the user. When using a mouse, "activation" typically starts when the user presses down the primary mouse button.
what is :nth-child in css | css nth child | how do i use nth child in css => The `:nth-child()` CSS pseudo-class matches elements based on the indexes of the elements in the child list of their parents. In other words, the `:nth-child()` selector selects child elements according to their position among all the sibling elements within a parent element.
what is :first-child in css | css first child | how do i use first child in css => The `:first-child` CSS pseudo-class represents the first element among a group of sibling elements.
what is :not in css | css not | how do i use not in css => The `:not()` CSS pseudo-class represents elements that do not match a list of selectors. Since it prevents specific items from being selected, it is known as the negation pseudo-class.
what is :root in css | css root | how do i use root in css => The `:root` CSS pseudo-class matches the root element of a tree representing the document. In HTML, `:root` represents the <html> element and is identical to the selector `html`, except that its specificity (0-1-0) is higher than html's (0-0-1).
what is ::before in css | css before | how do i use before in css => In CSS, `::before` creates a pseudo-element that is the first child of the selected element. It is often used to add cosmetic content to an element with the content property. It is inline by default.
what is ::after in css | css after | how do i use after in css => In CSS, `::after` creates a pseudo-element that is the last child of the selected element. It is often used to add cosmetic content to an element with the content property. It is inline by default.
what is :has in css | css has | how do i use has in css => The functional `:has()` CSS pseudo-class represents an element if any of the relative selectors that are passed as an argument match at least one element when anchored against this element.
what is class selectors in css | css class selectors | how do i use class selectors in css => The CSS class selector matches elements based on the contents of their `class` attribute.
what is id selectors in css | css id selectors | how do i use id selectors in css => The CSS ID selector matches an element based on the value of the element's `id` attribute. In order for the element to be selected, its `id` attribute must match exactly the value given in the selector.
what is universal selectors in css | css universal selectors | how do i use universal selectors in css => The CSS universal selector (`*`) matches elements of any type.
# tag: coding.web.html
what is the html tag in html | html html element | what does <html> do in html => The `<html>` HTML element represents the root (top-level element) of an HTML document, so it is also referred to as the root element. All other elements must be descendants of this element. There can be only one `<html>` element in a document.
what is the head tag in html | html head element | what does <head> do in html => The `<head>` HTML element contains machine-readable information (metadata) about the document, like its title, scripts, and style sheets. There can be only one `<head>` element in an HTML document.
what is the body tag in html | html body element | what does <body> do in html => The `<body>` HTML element represents the content of an HTML document. There can be only one `<body>` element in a document.
what is the title tag in html | html title element | what does <title> do in html => The `<title>` HTML element defines the document's title that is shown in a browser's title bar or a page's tab. It only contains text; HTML tags within the element, if any, are also treated as plain text.
what is the meta tag in html | html meta element | what does <meta> do in html => The `<meta>` HTML element represents metadata that cannot be represented by other meta-related elements, such as <base>, <link>, <script>, <style>, or <title>.
what is the link tag in html | html link element | what does <link> do in html => This element is most commonly used to link to stylesheets, but is also used to establish site icons (both "favicon" style icons and icons for the home screen and apps on mobile devices) among other things.
what is the script tag in html | html script element | what does <script> do in html => The `<script>` HTML element is used to embed executable code or data; this is typically used to embed or refer to JavaScript code. The `<script>` element can also be used with other languages, such as WebGL's GLSL shader programming language and JSON.
what is the style tag in html | html style element | what does <style> do in html => The `<style>` HTML element contains style information for a document, or part of a document. It contains CSS, which is applied to the contents of the document containing the `<style>` element.
what is the div tag in html | html div element | what does <div> do in html => The `<div>` HTML element is the generic container for flow content. It has no effect on the content or layout until styled in some way using CSS (e.g., styling is directly applied to it, or some kind of layout model like Flexbox is applied to its parent element).
what is the span tag in html | html span element | what does <span> do in html => The `<span>` HTML element is a generic inline container for phrasing content, which does not inherently represent anything. It can be used to group elements for styling purposes (using the `class` or `id` attributes), or because they share attribute values, such as `lang`. It should be used only when no other semantic element is appropriate.
what is the p tag in html | html p element | what does <p> do in html => The `<p>` HTML element represents a paragraph. Paragraphs are usually represented in visual media as blocks of text separated from adjacent blocks by blank lines and/or first-line indentation, but HTML paragraphs can be any structural grouping of related content, such as images or form fields.
what is the img tag in html | html img element | what does <img> do in html => The `<img>` HTML element embeds an image into the document.
what is the ul tag in html | html ul element | what does <ul> do in html => The `<ul>` HTML element represents an unordered list of items, typically rendered as a bulleted list.
what is the ol tag in html | html ol element | what does <ol> do in html => The `<ol>` HTML element represents an ordered list of items , typically rendered as a numbered list.
what is the li tag in html | html li element | what does <li> do in html => The `<li>` HTML element is used to represent an item in a list. It must be contained in a parent element: an ordered list (<ol>), an unordered list (<ul>), or a menu (<menu>). In menus and unordered lists, list items are usually displayed using bullet points.
what is the table tag in html | html table element | what does <table> do in html => The `<table>` HTML element represents tabular data, that is, information presented in a two-dimensional table comprised of rows and columns of cells containing data.
what is the tr tag in html | html tr element | what does <tr> do in html => The `<tr>` HTML element defines a row of cells in a table. The row's cells can then be established using a mix of <td> (data cell) and <th> (header cell) elements.
what is the td tag in html | html td element | what does <td> do in html => The `<td>` HTML element defines a cell of a table that contains data and may be used as a child of the <tr> element.
what is the th tag in html | html th element | what does <th> do in html => The `<th>` HTML element defines a cell as the header of a group of table cells and may be used as a child of the <tr> element. The exact nature of this group is defined by the `scope` and `headers` attributes.
what is the thead tag in html | html thead element | what does <thead> do in html => The `<thead>` HTML element encapsulates a set of table rows (<tr> elements), indicating that they comprise the head of a table with information about the table's columns. This is usually in the form of column headers (<th> elements).
what is the tbody tag in html | html tbody element | what does <tbody> do in html => The `<tbody>` HTML element encapsulates a set of table rows (<tr> elements), indicating that they comprise the body of a table's (main) data.
what is the form tag in html | html form element | what does <form> do in html => The `<form>` HTML element represents a document section containing interactive controls for submitting information. It is possible to use the and CSS pseudo-classes to style a `<form>` element based on whether the elements inside the form are valid.
what is the input tag in html | html input element | what does <input> do in html => The `<input>` HTML element is used to create interactive controls for web-based forms in order to accept data from the user; a wide variety of types of input data and control widgets are available, depending on the device and user agent.
what is the button tag in html | html button element | what does <button> do in html => The `<button>` HTML element is an interactive element activated by a user with a mouse, keyboard, finger, voice command, or other assistive technology. Once activated, it then performs an action, such as submitting a form or opening a dialog.
what is the label tag in html | html label element | what does <label> do in html => The `<label>` HTML element represents a caption for an item in a user interface.
what is the select tag in html | html select element | what does <select> do in html => The `<select>` HTML element represents a control that provides a menu of options.
what is the option tag in html | html option element | what does <option> do in html => The `<option>` HTML element is used to define an item contained in a <select>, an <optgroup>, or a <datalist> element. As such, `<option>` can represent menu items in popups and other lists of items in an HTML document.
what is the textarea tag in html | html textarea element | what does <textarea> do in html => The `<textarea>` HTML element represents a multi-line plain-text editing control, useful when you want to allow users to enter a sizeable amount of free-form text, for example a comment on a review or feedback form.
what is the br tag in html | html br element | what does <br> do in html => The `<br>` HTML element produces a line break in text (carriage-return). It is useful for writing a poem or an address, where the division of lines is significant.
what is the hr tag in html | html hr element | what does <hr> do in html => The `<hr>` HTML element represents a thematic break between elements: for example, a change of scene in a story, or a shift of topic within a section.
what is the strong tag in html | html strong element | what does <strong> do in html => The `<strong>` HTML element indicates that its contents have strong importance, seriousness, or urgency. Browsers typically render the contents in bold type.
what is the em tag in html | html em element | what does <em> do in html => The `<em>` HTML element marks text that has stress emphasis. The `<em>` element can be nested, with each level of nesting indicating a greater degree of emphasis.
what is the b tag in html | html b element | what does <b> do in html => The `<b>` HTML element is used to draw the reader's attention to the element's contents, which are not otherwise granted special importance. This was formerly known as the Boldface element, and most browsers still draw the text in boldface. However, you should not use `<b>` for styling text or granting importance.
what is the section tag in html | html section element | what does <section> do in html => The `<section>` HTML element represents a generic standalone section of a document, which doesn't have a more specific semantic element to represent it. Sections should always have a heading, with very few exceptions.
what is the article tag in html | html article element | what does <article> do in html => The `<article>` HTML element represents a self-contained composition in a document, page, application, or site, which is intended to be independently distributable or reusable (e.g., in syndication).
what is the nav tag in html | html nav element | what does <nav> do in html => Common examples of navigation sections are menus, tables of contents, and indexes.
what is the header tag in html | html header element | what does <header> do in html => The `<header>` HTML element represents introductory content, typically a group of introductory or navigational aids. It may contain some heading elements but also a logo, a search form, an author name, and other elements.
what is the footer tag in html | html footer element | what does <footer> do in html => The `<footer>` HTML element represents a footer for its nearest ancestor sectioning content or sectioning root element. A `<footer>` typically contains information about the author of the section, copyright data or links to related documents.
what is the main tag in html | html main element | what does <main> do in html => The `<main>` HTML element represents the dominant content of the <body> of a document. The main content area consists of content that is directly related to or expands upon the central topic of a document, or the central functionality of an application.
what is the aside tag in html | html aside element | what does <aside> do in html => The `<aside>` HTML element represents a portion of a document whose content is only indirectly related to the document's main content. Asides are frequently presented as sidebars or call-out boxes.
what is the figure tag in html | html figure element | what does <figure> do in html => The `<figure>` HTML element represents self-contained content, potentially with an optional caption, which is specified using the <figcaption> element. The figure, its caption, and its contents are referenced as a single unit.
what is the figcaption tag in html | html figcaption element | what does <figcaption> do in html => The `<figcaption>` HTML element represents a caption or legend describing the rest of the contents of its parent <figure> element, providing the `<figure>` an accessible name.
what is the video tag in html | html video element | what does <video> do in html => The `<video>` HTML element embeds a media player which supports video playback into the document. You can use `<video>` for audio content as well, but the <audio> element may provide a more appropriate user experience.
what is the audio tag in html | html audio element | what does <audio> do in html => The `<audio>` HTML element is used to embed sound content in documents. It may contain one or more audio sources, represented using the `src` attribute or the <source> element: the browser will choose the most suitable one. It can also be the destination for streamed media, using a MediaStream.
what is the source tag in html | html source element | what does <source> do in html => The `<source>` HTML element specifies one or more media resources for the <picture>, <audio>, and <video> elements. It is a void element, which means that it has no content and does not require a closing tag.
what is the canvas tag in html | html canvas element | what does <canvas> do in html => Use the HTML `<canvas>` element with either the canvas scripting API or the WebGL API to draw graphics and animations.
what is the pre tag in html | html pre element | what does <pre> do in html => The `<pre>` HTML element represents preformatted text which is to be presented exactly as written in the HTML file. The text is typically rendered using a non-proportional, or monospaced font.
what is the code tag in html | html code element | what does <code> do in html => The `<code>` HTML element displays its contents styled in a fashion intended to indicate that the text is a short fragment of computer code. By default, the content text is displayed using the user agent's default monospace font.
what is the blockquote tag in html | html blockquote element | what does <blockquote> do in html => The `<blockquote>` HTML element indicates that the enclosed text is an extended quotation. Usually, this is rendered visually by indentation (see Notes for how to change it). A URL for the source of the quotation may be given using the `cite` attribute, while a text representation of the source can be given using the <cite> element.
what is the details tag in html | html details element | what does <details> do in html => The `<details>` HTML element creates a disclosure widget in which information is visible only when the widget is toggled into an open state. A summary or label must be provided using the <summary> element.
what is the summary tag in html | html summary element | what does <summary> do in html => The `<summary>` HTML element specifies a summary, caption, or legend for a <details> element's disclosure box. Clicking the `<summary>` element toggles the state of the parent `<details>` element open and closed.
what is the dialog tag in html | html dialog element | what does <dialog> do in html => The `<dialog>` HTML element represents a modal or non-modal dialog box or other interactive component, such as a dismissible alert, inspector, or subwindow.
what is the template tag in html | html template element | what does <template> do in html => The `<template>` HTML element serves as a mechanism for holding HTML fragments, which can either be used later via JavaScript, generated immediately and inserted into a shadow DOM, or used as part of out-of-order patching with `<template for="...">`.
what is the slot tag in html | html slot element | what does <slot> do in html => The `<slot>` HTML element is a placeholder inside a Web Component that you can fill with your own markup when the component is used. This lets you create separate DOM trees and present them together.
what is the progress tag in html | html progress element | what does <progress> do in html => The `<progress>` HTML element displays an indicator showing the completion progress of a task, typically displayed as a progress bar.
what is the meter tag in html | html meter element | what does <meter> do in html => The `<meter>` HTML element represents either a scalar value within a known range or a fractional value.
what is the abbr tag in html | html abbr element | what does <abbr> do in html => The `<abbr>` HTML element represents an abbreviation or acronym. When including an abbreviation or acronym, provide a full expansion of the term in plain text on first use, along with the `<abbr>` to mark up the abbreviation. This informs the user what the abbreviation or acronym means.
what is the small tag in html | html small element | what does <small> do in html => The `<small>` HTML element represents side-comments and small print, like copyright and legal text, independent of its styled presentation. By default, it renders text within it one font-size smaller, such as from `small` to `x-small`.
what is the sub tag in html | html sub element | what does <sub> do in html => The `<sub>` HTML element specifies inline text which should be displayed as subscript for solely typographical reasons. Subscripts are typically rendered with a lowered baseline using smaller text.
what is the sup tag in html | html sup element | what does <sup> do in html => The `<sup>` HTML element specifies inline text which is to be displayed as superscript for solely typographical reasons. Superscripts are usually rendered with a raised baseline using smaller text.
what is the mark tag in html | html mark element | what does <mark> do in html => The `<mark>` HTML element represents text which is marked or highlighted for reference or notation purposes due to the marked passage's relevance in the enclosing context.
what is the time tag in html | html time element | what does <time> do in html => The `<time>` HTML element represents a specific period in time. It may include the `datetime` attribute to translate dates into machine-readable format, allowing for better search engine results or custom features such as reminders.
what is the address tag in html | html address element | what does <address> do in html => The `<address>` HTML element indicates that the enclosed HTML provides contact information for a person or people, or for an organization.
what is the fieldset tag in html | html fieldset element | what does <fieldset> do in html => The `<fieldset>` HTML element is used to group several controls as well as labels (<label>) within a web form.
