what is the legend tag in html | html legend element | what does <legend> do in html => The `<legend>` HTML element represents a caption for the content of its parent <fieldset>. In customizable `<select>` elements, the `<legend>` element is allowed as a child of `<optgroup>`, to provide a label that is easy to target and style. This replaces any text set in the `<optgroup>` element's `label` attribute, and it has the same semantics.
what is the datalist tag in html | html datalist element | what does <datalist> do in html => The `<datalist>` HTML element contains a set of <option> elements that represent the permissible or recommended options available to choose from within other controls.
what is the picture tag in html | html picture element | what does <picture> do in html => The `<picture>` HTML element contains zero or more <source> elements and one <img> element to offer alternative versions of an image for different display/device scenarios.
what is the base tag in html | html base element | what does <base> do in html => The `<base>` HTML element specifies the base URL to use for all relative URLs in a document. There can be only one `<base>` element in a document.
what is the class attribute in html | html class attribute | how do i use the class attribute => The `class` global attribute is a list of the classes of the element, separated by ASCII whitespace.
what is the id attribute in html | html id attribute | how do i use the id attribute => The `id` global attribute defines an identifier (ID) that must be unique within the entire document.
what is the style attribute in html | html style attribute | how do i use the style attribute => The `style` global attribute contains CSS styling declarations to be applied to the element. Note that it is recommended for styles to be defined in a separate file or files. This attribute and the <style> element have mainly the purpose of allowing for quick styling, for example for testing purposes.
what is the hidden attribute in html | html hidden attribute | how do i use the hidden attribute => The `hidden` global attribute is an enumerated attribute indicating that the browser should not render the contents of the element. For example, it can be used to hide elements of the page that can't be used until the login process has been completed.
what is the tabindex attribute in html | html tabindex attribute | how do i use the tabindex attribute => The `tabindex` global attribute allows developers to make HTML elements focusable, allow or prevent them from being sequentially focusable (usually with the <kbd>Tab</kbd> key, hence the name) and determine their relative ordering for sequential focus navigation.
what is the title attribute in html | html title attribute | how do i use the title attribute => The `title` global attribute contains text representing advisory information related to the element it belongs to.
what is the lang attribute in html | html lang attribute | how do i use the lang attribute => The `lang` global attribute helps define the language of an element: the language that non-editable elements are written in, or the language that the editable elements should be written in by the user. The attribute contains a single BCP 47 language tag.
# tag: coding.web.dom
what is document.queryselector in javascript | what does queryselector do in javascript | js queryselector => The Document method `querySelector()` returns the first Element within the document that matches the specified CSS selector, or group of CSS selectors. If no matches are found, `null` is returned.
what is document.queryselectorall in javascript | what does queryselectorall do in javascript | js queryselectorall => The Document method `querySelectorAll()` returns a static (not live) NodeList representing a list of the document's elements that match the specified group of selectors.
what is document.getelementbyid in javascript | what does getelementbyid do in javascript | js getelementbyid => The `getElementById()` method of the Document interface returns an Element object representing the element whose id property matches the specified string. Since element IDs are required to be unique if specified, they're a useful way to get access to a specific element quickly.
what is document.createelement in javascript | what does createelement do in javascript | js createelement => The `createElement()` method of the Document interface creates a new HTMLElement that has the specified `localName`. If `localName` isn't recognized, the method creates an HTMLUnknownElement.
what is document.getelementsbyclassname in javascript | what does getelementsbyclassname do in javascript | js getelementsbyclassname => The `getElementsByClassName` method of Document interface returns an array-like object of all child elements which have all of the given class name(s).
what is document.title in javascript | what does title do in javascript | js title => When present, it defaults to the value of the `<title>`.
what is document.domcontentloaded event in javascript | what does domcontentloaded event do in javascript | js domcontentloaded event => The `DOMContentLoaded` event fires when the HTML document has been completely parsed, and all deferred scripts (`<script defer src="…">` and `<script type="module">`) have downloaded and executed. It doesn't wait for other things like images, subframes, and async scripts to finish loading.
what is node.appendchild in javascript | what does appendchild do in javascript | js appendchild => The `appendChild()` method of the Node interface adds a node to the end of the list of children of a specified parent node. If the given child is a DocumentFragment, the entire contents of the DocumentFragment are moved into the child list of the specified parent node.
what is node.removechild in javascript | what does removechild do in javascript | js removechild => The `removeChild()` method of the Node interface removes a child node from the DOM and returns the removed node. Unlike the return value preserves the `EventListener` objects associated with it.
what is node.textcontent in javascript | what does textcontent do in javascript | js textcontent => The `textContent` property of the Node interface represents the text content of the node and its descendants.
what is node.parentnode in javascript | what does parentnode do in javascript | js parentnode => The read-only `parentNode` property of the Node interface returns the parent of the specified node in the DOM tree. `Document` and `DocumentFragment` nodes can never have a parent, so `parentNode` will always return `null`. It also returns `null` if the node has just been created and is not yet attached to the tree.
what is element.innerhtml in javascript | what does innerhtml do in javascript | js innerhtml => The `innerHTML` property of the Element interface gets or sets the HTML or XML markup contained within the element, omitting any shadow roots in both cases.
what is element.classlist in javascript | what does classlist do in javascript | js classlist => The read-only `classList` property of the Element interface contains a live DOMTokenList collection representing the `class` attribute of the element. This can then be used to manipulate the class list.
what is element.setattribute in javascript | what does setattribute do in javascript | js setattribute => The `setAttribute()` method of the Element interface sets the value of an attribute on the specified element. If the attribute already exists, the value is updated; otherwise a new attribute is added with the specified name and value.
what is element.getattribute in javascript | what does getattribute do in javascript | js getattribute => The `getAttribute()` method of the Element interface returns the string value of the specified attribute of the specified element. It returns `null` if the element doesn't have an attribute with the given name.
what is element.remove in javascript | what does remove do in javascript | js remove => The `remove()` method of the Element interface removes the element from its parent node. Nothing happens if parentNode is `null`.
what is element.append in javascript | what does append do in javascript | js append => The `Element.append()` method inserts a set of Node objects or strings after the last child of the `Element`. Strings are inserted as equivalent Text nodes.
what is element.closest in javascript | what does closest do in javascript | js closest => The `closest()` method of the Element interface traverses the element and its parents (heading toward the document root) until it finds a node that matches the specified CSS selector.
what is element.keydown event in javascript | what does keydown event do in javascript | js keydown event => The `keydown` event is fired when a key is pressed. Unlike the deprecated keypress event, the `keydown` event is fired for all keys, regardless of whether they produce a character value.
what is element.scrollintoview in javascript | what does scrollintoview do in javascript | js scrollintoview => The `scrollIntoView()` method of the Element interface scrolls the element's ancestor containers such that the element on which `scrollIntoView()` is called is visible to the user.
what is element.getboundingclientrect in javascript | what does getboundingclientrect do in javascript | js getboundingclientrect => The `Element.getBoundingClientRect()` method returns a DOMRect object providing information about the size of an element and its position relative to the viewport.
what is htmlelement.style in javascript | what does style do in javascript | js style => The read-only `style` property of the HTMLElement interface returns the inline `style` of an element in the form of a live CSSStyleProperties object. This object can be used to get and set the inline styles of an element.
what is htmlelement.dataset in javascript | what does dataset do in javascript | js dataset => The `dataset` read-only property of the HTMLElement interface provides read/write access to custom data attributes (`data-*`) on elements. It exposes a map of strings (DOMStringMap) with an entry for each `data-*` attribute.
what is htmlelement.hidden in javascript | what does hidden do in javascript | js hidden => The HTMLElement property `hidden` reflects the value of the element's `hidden` attribute.
what is htmlelement.focus in javascript | what does focus do in javascript | js focus => The `HTMLElement.focus()` method sets focus on the specified element, if it can be focused. The focused element is the element that will receive keyboard and similar events by default.
what is htmlinputelement.value in javascript | what does value do in javascript | js value => This property can also be set directly, for example to set a default value based on some condition.
what is eventtarget.addeventlistener in javascript | what does addeventlistener do in javascript | js addeventlistener => The `addEventListener()` method of the EventTarget interface sets up a function that will be called whenever the specified event is delivered to the target.
what is eventtarget.removeeventlistener in javascript | what does removeeventlistener do in javascript | js removeeventlistener => The `removeEventListener()` method of the EventTarget interface removes an event listener previously registered with from the target.
what is event.preventdefault in javascript | what does preventdefault do in javascript | js preventdefault => The `preventDefault()` method of the Event interface tells the user agent that the event is being explicitly handled, so its default action, such as page scrolling, link navigation, or pasting text, should not be taken.
what is event.stoppropagation in javascript | what does stoppropagation do in javascript | js stoppropagation => It does not, however, prevent any default behaviors from occurring; for instance, clicks on links are still processed. If you want to stop those behaviors, see the method. If you want to stop those, see .
what is event.target in javascript | what does target do in javascript | js target => The read-only `target` property of the Event interface is a reference to the object onto which the event was dispatched. It is different from Event.currentTarget when the event handler is called during the bubbling or capturing phase of the event.
what is window.settimeout in javascript | what does settimeout do in javascript | js settimeout => The `setTimeout()` method of the Window interface sets a timer which executes a function or specified piece of code once the timer expires.
what is window.setinterval in javascript | what does setinterval do in javascript | js setinterval => The `setInterval()` method of the Window interface repeatedly calls a function or executes a code snippet, with a fixed time delay between each call.
what is window.cleartimeout in javascript | what does cleartimeout do in javascript | js cleartimeout => The `clearTimeout()` method of the Window interface cancels a timeout previously established by calling . If the parameter provided does not identify a previously established action, this method does nothing.
what is window.clearinterval in javascript | what does clearinterval do in javascript | js clearinterval => The `clearInterval()` method of the Window interface cancels a timed, repeating action which was previously established by a call to . If the parameter provided does not identify a previously established action, this method does nothing.
what is window.requestanimationframe in javascript | what does requestanimationframe do in javascript | js requestanimationframe => The `window.requestAnimationFrame()` method tells the browser you wish to perform an animation. It requests the browser to call a user-supplied callback function before the next repaint.
what is window.fetch in javascript | what does fetch do in javascript | js fetch => The `fetch()` method of the Window interface starts the process of fetching a resource from the network, returning a promise that is fulfilled once the response is available.
what is window.localstorage in javascript | what does localstorage do in javascript | js localstorage => The `localStorage` read-only property of the window interface allows you to access a Storage object for the Document's origin; the stored data is saved across browser sessions.
what is window.sessionstorage in javascript | what does sessionstorage do in javascript | js sessionstorage => `sessionStorage` is similar to localStorage; the difference is that while `localStorage` is partitioned by origin only, `sessionStorage` is partitioned by both origin and browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts). The data in `sessionStorage` is only kept for the duration of the page session.
what is window.alert in javascript | what does alert do in javascript | js alert => `window.alert()` instructs the browser to display a dialog with an optional message, and to wait until the user dismisses the dialog. Under some conditions , for example, when the user switches tabs , the browser may not actually display a dialog, or may not wait for the user to dismiss the dialog.
what is window.confirm in javascript | what does confirm do in javascript | js confirm => `window.confirm()` instructs the browser to display a dialog with an optional message, and to wait until the user either confirms or cancels the dialog. Under some conditions , for example, when the user switches tabs , the browser may not actually display a dialog, or may not wait for the user to confirm or cancel the dialog.
what is window.prompt in javascript | what does prompt do in javascript | js prompt => `window.prompt()` instructs the browser to display a dialog with an optional message prompting the user to input some text, and to wait until the user either submits the text or cancels the dialog.
what is window.open in javascript | what does open do in javascript | js open => The `open()` method of the `Window` interface loads a specified resource into a new or existing browsing context (that is, a tab, a window, or an iframe) under a specified name.
what is window.innerwidth in javascript | what does innerwidth do in javascript | js innerwidth => The read-only Window property `innerWidth` returns the interior width of the window in pixels (that is, the width of the window's layout viewport). That includes the width of the vertical scroll bar, if one is present.
what is window.scrollto in javascript | what does scrollto do in javascript | js scrollto => The `scrollTo()` method of the Window interface scrolls to a particular set of coordinates in the document.
what is window.load event in javascript | what does load event do in javascript | js load event => The `load` event is fired when the whole page has loaded, including all dependent resources such as stylesheets, scripts (including async, deferred, and module scripts), iframes, and images, except those that are loaded lazily.
what is window.resize event in javascript | what does resize event do in javascript | js resize event => The `resize` event fires when the document view (window) has been resized. This event is not cancelable and does not bubble. In some earlier browsers it was possible to register `resize` event handlers on any HTML element.
what is console.log in javascript | what does log do in javascript | js log => The `console.log()` static method outputs a message to the console.
what is console.error in javascript | js error => The `console.error()` static method outputs a message to the console at the "error" log level. The message is only displayed to the user if the console is configured to display error output. In most cases, the log level is configured within the console UI. The message may be formatted as an error, with red colors and call stack information.
what is console.warn in javascript | what does warn do in javascript | js warn => The `console.warn()` static method outputs a warning message to the console at the "warning" log level. The message is only displayed to the user if the console is configured to display warning output. In most cases, the log level is configured within the console UI. The message may receive special formatting, such as yellow colors and a warning icon.
what is console.table in javascript | what does table do in javascript | js table => The `console.table()` static method displays tabular data as a table.
what is storage.setitem in javascript | what does setitem do in javascript | js setitem => The `setItem()` method of the Storage interface, when passed a key name and value, will add that key to the given `Storage` object, or update that key's value if it already exists.
what is storage.getitem in javascript | what does getitem do in javascript | js getitem => The `getItem()` method of the Storage interface, when passed a key name, will return that key's value, or `null` if the key does not exist, in the given `Storage` object.
what is storage.removeitem in javascript | what does removeitem do in javascript | js removeitem => The `removeItem()` method of the Storage interface, when passed a key name, will remove that key from the given `Storage` object if it exists. The `Storage` interface of the Web Storage API provides access to a particular domain's session or local storage.
what is response.json in javascript | js json => The `json()` method of the Response interface takes a Response stream and reads it to completion. It returns a promise which resolves with the result of parsing the body text as JSON.
what is response.ok in javascript | what does ok do in javascript | js ok => The `ok` read-only property of the Response interface contains a Boolean stating whether the response was successful (status in the range 200-299) or not.
what is response.status in javascript | what does status do in javascript | js status => The `status` read-only property of the Response interface contains the HTTP status code of the response.

It is used for drawing shapes, text, images, and other objects.

what is geolocation api in javascript | what does geolocation api do in javascript | js geolocation api => The Geolocation API allows the user to provide their location to web applications if they so desire. For privacy reasons, the user is asked for permission to report location information.

what is intersectionobserver in javascript | what does intersectionobserver do in javascript | js intersectionobserver => The `IntersectionObserver` interface of the Intersection Observer API provides a way to asynchronously observe changes in the intersection of a target element with an ancestor element or with a top-level document's . what is web workers api in javascript | what does web workers api do in javascript | js web workers api => Web Workers makes it possible to run a script operation in a background thread separate from the main execution thread of a web application. The advantage of this is that laborious processing can be performed in a separate thread, allowing the main (usually the UI) thread to run without being blocked/slowed down.
what is indexeddb api in javascript | what does indexeddb api do in javascript | js indexeddb api => IndexedDB is a low-level API for client-side storage of significant amounts of structured data, including files/blobs. This API uses indexes to enable high-performance searches of this data. While Web Storage is useful for storing smaller amounts of data, it is less useful for storing larger amounts of structured data. IndexedDB provides a solution.

what is gamepad api in javascript | what does gamepad api do in javascript | js gamepad api => The Gamepad API is a way for developers to access and respond to signals from gamepads and other game controllers in a simple, consistent way.
what is fullscreen api in javascript | what does fullscreen api do in javascript | js fullscreen api => The Fullscreen API adds methods to present a specific Element (and its descendants) in fullscreen mode, and to exit fullscreen mode once it is no longer needed.

what is blob in javascript | what does blob do in javascript | js blob => The `Blob` interface represents a blob, which is a file-like object of immutable, raw data; they can be read as text or binary data, or converted into a ReadableStream so its methods can be used for processing the data.
what is filereader in javascript | what does filereader do in javascript | js filereader => The `FileReader` interface lets web applications asynchronously read the contents of files (or raw data buffers) stored on the user's computer, using File or Blob objects to specify the file or data to read.
what is customevent in javascript | what does customevent do in javascript | js customevent => The `CustomEvent` interface can be used to attach custom data to an event generated by an application. As an alternative to `CustomEvent`, you can subclass the `Event` interface to add custom data and behavior.
what is mutationobserver in javascript | what does mutationobserver do in javascript | js mutationobserver => The `MutationObserver` interface provides the ability to watch for changes being made to the DOM tree. It is designed as a replacement for the older Mutation Events feature, which was part of the DOM3 Events specification.
what is performance.now in javascript | what does now do in javascript | js now => The `performance.now()` method returns a high resolution timestamp in milliseconds. It represents the time elapsed since Performance.timeOrigin (the time when navigation has started in window contexts, or the time when the worker is run in Worker and ServiceWorker contexts).
what is crypto.randomuuid in javascript | what does randomuuid do in javascript | js randomuuid => The `randomUUID()` method of the Crypto interface is used to generate a v4 UUID using a cryptographically secure random number generator.
what is broadcastchannel in javascript | what does broadcastchannel do in javascript | js broadcastchannel => The `BroadcastChannel` interface represents a named channel that any browsing context of a given origin can subscribe to. It allows communication between different documents (in different windows, tabs, frames or iframes) of the same origin.
what is serial in javascript | what does serial do in javascript | js serial => The `Serial` interface of the Web Serial API provides attributes and methods for finding and connecting to serial ports from a web page.
what is webgl api in javascript | what does webgl api do in javascript | js webgl api => WebGL (Web Graphics Library) is a JavaScript API for rendering high-performance interactive 3D and 2D graphics within any compatible web browser without the use of plug-ins. WebGL does so by introducing an API that closely conforms to OpenGL ES 2.0 that can be used in HTML <canvas> elements.
what is webgpu api in javascript | what does webgpu api do in javascript | js webgpu api => The WebGPU API enables web developers to use the underlying system's GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) to carry out high-performance computations and draw complex images that can be rendered in the browser.
what is history api in javascript | what does history api do in javascript | js history api => The History API provides access to the browser's session history (not to be confused with WebExtensions history) through the history global object. It exposes useful methods and properties that let you navigate back and forth through the user's history, and manipulate the contents of the history stack.
what is service worker api in javascript | what does service worker api do in javascript | js service worker api => Service workers essentially act as proxy servers that sit between web applications, the browser, and the network (when available).
